sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
The appeal is filed by the appellant - United India Insurance Company Limited, who is the insurer of the tempo bearing No.KA-19-A-4167 challenging the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

2. The brief facts of the case are that the claimant has sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 01.10.2006 at about 12.15 p.m., on NH-17, near Gopady Bus Stand, Gopady Village,
Kundapura Taluk, between the vehicles i.e., TVS XL Moped bearing No.KA- 20-R-4091, bus bearing No.KA-20-A-5769 (offending vehicle) and 407 tempo bearing No.KA-19-A-4167 (offending vehicle).
Therefore, the claimant has preferred claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act, seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
4.
Learned counsel for the appellant/United India Insurance Company Limited submitted that the driver of the bus was also rash and negligent in causing the accident but he was exonerated.
Therefore, submitted equal percentage of negligence is to be attributed on the part of the driver of the bus considering the scenario of the accident.
Therefore, prays for modification of the judgment and award in this regard.
5. Learned counsel for the respondents justified the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

6. In the present case, upon perusal of the complaint, the claimant was riding his TVS XL Moped No.KA-20-R-4091, at that time, the driver of the 407 tempo bearing No.KA-19-A-4167 came with high speed and dashed the claimant's TVS XL Moped.
Resultantly, the claimant fell on the road then the driver of the bus bearing No.KA-20-A-5769 moved the bus and ran over on the right hand of the claimant.

Therefore, in this regard, due to the hit of the tempo, the claimant had sustained some injuries and if the bus had not moved on the hand of the claimant, then the nature of the injuries would have been different only because of the hit by the tempo, but because of the hit by the tempo and bus, the claimant had sustained more grievous injuries.
Even though, initially, the tempo driver was rash and negligent, the bus driver was also expected to drive the bus with care and caution.
Even though the initial cause was a hit by tempo, if the bus had not run over the claimant, then the claimant would have sustained less injuries only because of the tempo's hit.

Therefore, in this regard, both the drivers have contributed rash and negligence in causing the accident, but the Tribunal has committed an error in fastening 90% of the rashness on the part of the driver of the tempo and 10% on the claimant and exonerating the driver of the bus.
This is to be re-appreciated upon the evidence on record.
Upon considering the evidence on record, the claimant had sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of both the tempo and bus.

sentences.text: Therefore, this also shows that the driver of the bus was rash and negligent.
Therefore, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal so far as holding rash and negligent aspects is concerned needs to be modified considering the scenario of the accident.
As revealed from the evidence, both the drivers of the tempo and the driver of the bus have equally contributed to the accident.
There is no evidence to prove that the claimant has also contributed his negligence while riding his TVS XL Moped.

Therefore, regarding the rash and negligent aspect, the judgment and award modified that it is held that the driver of the 407 tempo No.KA-19-A-4167 was 50% rash and negligent and driver of the bus No.KA-20-A-5769 was 50% rash and negligent.
The 10% negligence attributed on the part of the claimant is set-aside.
7. The Tribunal has quantified the compensation of Rs.9,75,000/- under the various heads.

Therefore, the claimant is entitled a full of compensation of Rs.9,75,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization equally from both the owner and insurer of the tempo and bus.
8. Thus, the owner and insurer of the 407 tempo and the bus are jointly and severally pay compensation as determined by the Tribunal in the ratio of 50:50.
9. The other observations are kept in tact.
Therefore, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company is liable to be allowed-in-part.

10. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.123/2007 is hereby modified holding the claimant is entitled for full compensation of Rs.9,75,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
iii. The owner and insurer of the 407 tempo and bus respectively are jointly and severally pay above determined compensation in the ratio of 50:50 to the claimant.
iv. Costs made easy.
v. Draw award accordingly.
vi. The amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted  to the Tribunal forthwith.
vii. Registry is directed return the Trial Court Records along with certified copy of this order without delay.
